2027-04-04.title: New Sunday · The Lord Appears to Thomas
readings: Peace be with you; receive the Holy Spirit
Elijah taken up; Elisha receives his spirit
The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God
Here is your God; he will feed his flock
A living hope through the resurrection
Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead
2027-04-04.alt: New Sunday, the first Sunday after Qyomtho.
2027-04-04.verse: Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”
theo: On the evening of Easter the disciples are behind locked doors, afraid. Jesus comes and stands among them: “Peace be with you.” He shows them his hands and side, and they rejoice. Then he sends them: “As the Father has sent me, so I send you,” breathes on them and says, “Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them.” From the first Easter evening the risen Lord gives his Church peace, mission, the Spirit and the power to forgive sins.

Thomas was not there. When the others say, “We have seen the Lord,” he answers: “Unless I see the mark of the nails in his hands, and put my finger in the mark of the nails and my hand in his side, I will not believe.” A week later Jesus comes again and says: “Put your finger here and see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it in my side. Do not doubt but believe.” And Thomas makes the greatest confession of faith in the Gospels: “My Lord and my God!”

For us in India this Gospel is our own story. Thomas, who doubted and then believed, brought that faith to our land. The Church of Malankara, like all the St Thomas Christians, received from him the confession “My Lord and my God.” His doubt became our certainty; his wounded hand-touch became our faith.

Jesus adds a word for all later generations: “Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.” That is us. St Peter says: “Although you have not seen him, you love him… and rejoice with an indescribable and glorious joy.” New Sunday asks: do we live with the joy of believers, or with the fear of locked doors?
conn: The breath of life.
As God breathed into Adam (Genesis 2:7), the risen Christ breathes the Spirit into his disciples: a new creation.
Elijah and Elisha.
Elisha asks for a double share of Elijah's spirit (2 Kings 2:9); the apostles receive the Spirit of the risen Lord.
Joseph raised up.
Joseph, rejected by his brothers, is raised over Egypt to save them (Genesis 41): a figure of the risen Christ.
The wounds remain.
The risen body keeps its wounds: signs of love that last for ever (Revelation 5:6).
altar: Thomas touched the wounds; we receive the wounded and risen Body at the Holy Qurbono. Many in our tradition whisper Thomas' words at the elevation: “My Lord and my God.”
outline: The risen Lord's first gifts to his Church.
Honest questions brought to Jesus become faith.
St Thomas and the faith of India: “My Lord and my God.”
Point 4 · Blessed are those who have not seen
live: Pray Thomas' prayer
At the elevation in Holy Qurbono, and each morning, say: “My Lord and my God.”
Receive his peace (John 20:19)
Bring a fear or a locked door of your heart to Jesus in Confession.
Share your faith
Tell one person how you came to believe.
fathers: The disbelief of Thomas was of more benefit to our faith than the faith of the believing disciples; when he touched and believed, every doubt was removed from our minds (Homilies on the Gospels 26).
He saw and touched the man, and confessed the God whom he did not see and touch (Tractates on John 121).
magis: Catechism 644–645
The apostles' faith was born of the encounter with the risen Lord; Jesus invited them to touch his body, which kept the marks of the Passion.
Catechism 1441–1442
The risen Christ gave the apostles the power to forgive sins in his name.
Catechism 448
The title “Lord” confesses the divinity of Jesus; Thomas' confession is its high point.
saints: Hevoro week ends. 11 April: the Second Sunday after Qyomtho.
2027-04-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, risen and wounded, you came through locked doors and gave your disciples peace. Breathe your Spirit on us, heal our doubts, and make us confess with St Thomas, our father in faith: My Lord and my God! Amen.

2027-04-11.title: Second Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: Do you love me? Feed my sheep
The song of Moses at the sea
God raised him from the dead
Pray in the Spirit at all times
The risen Lord by the Sea of Tiberias
2027-04-11.verse: Jesus said to them, “Come and have breakfast.”
theo: After the Resurrection Peter says, “I am going fishing,” and the others go with him. They fish all night and catch nothing. At dawn a stranger on the shore says: “Cast the net to the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” The net fills so full they cannot haul it in. The beloved disciple says: “It is the Lord!” Peter jumps into the sea to reach him.

On the shore Jesus has already made a charcoal fire, with fish and bread. “Come and have breakfast.” The risen Lord of glory cooks for his tired friends. He meets them in their ordinary work, in their failure, and feeds them. Every Holy Qurbono is this breakfast on the shore: the risen Lord takes bread and gives it to us.

Then, beside another charcoal fire, Jesus heals Peter's wound. Three times Peter had denied him by a fire in the high priest's courtyard; three times Jesus asks: “Simon son of John, do you love me?” Three times Peter answers: “Lord, you know that I love you.” And three times Jesus entrusts him: “Feed my lambs… tend my sheep… feed my sheep.” Failure is not the end; love restores and sends.

Moses sang at the sea: “The LORD is my strength and my might, and he has become my salvation.” Wisdom says: “God did not make death.” Paul preaches in Antioch: “God raised him from the dead.” The risen Christ turns empty nights into full nets, and denials into love.
conn: The full net.
153 large fish (John 21:11): the Fathers saw in the unbroken net the Church gathering all nations without being torn.
Two charcoal fires.
Peter denied Jesus by a charcoal fire (John 18:18) and is restored by another (John 21:9).
The song of the sea.
Exodus 15: the first Easter song, sung after passing through the waters, as we pass through Baptism.
God did not make death.
Wisdom 1:13; God created for life, and in Christ restores it.
altar: “Come and have breakfast.” Jesus “took the bread and gave it to them” (John 21:13): the same gestures as at the Last Supper and Emmaus. At every Qurbono the risen Lord invites us to his table on the shore.
outline: The risen Lord serves and feeds: the Eucharist.
Peter restored; our failures healed by love.
Love becomes service: pray for our pastors.
“Lord, you know that I love you.”
live: Answer the question
Each night this week answer Jesus: “Lord, you know that I love you.”
Begin again
Return to a good practice you abandoned after a failure.
Pray for the Pope and bishops
Pray for Peter's successor and our Catholicos, shepherds of the flock.
fathers: The threefold confession of love answers the threefold denial, so that his tongue might serve love no less than fear (Tractates on John 123).
The disciples returned to fishing, which was not sin; but the Lord met them at their work, to show that he calls us in the midst of our daily labour (Homilies on the Gospels 24).
magis: Catechism 553, 881
Jesus entrusted to Peter a specific authority: to feed his sheep; the Pope is Peter's successor.
Catechism 1429
Peter's conversion after his triple denial bears witness to Jesus' infinite mercy.
Catechism 1347
The Eucharistic meals with the risen Lord (Emmaus, the shore) are signs of his presence.
saints: Weekdays of the season of Qyomtho. 18 April: III Sunday after Qyomtho.
2027-04-11.prayer: Risen Lord, you met your disciples after a night of failure, filled their nets and fed them on the shore. Feed us at your table, heal our denials with your love, and send us to care for your flock. Lord, you know that we love you. Amen.

2027-04-18.title: Third Sunday after Qyomtho · The Road to Emmaus
readings: He appeared in another form to two of them
Yet you did not return to me
I was ready to be found
By grace you have been saved
2027-04-18.verse: Were not our hearts burning within us while he was talking to us on the road, while he was opening the scriptures to us?
theo: On Easter afternoon two disciples walk away from Jerusalem towards Emmaus, sad and confused. “We had hoped that he was the one to redeem Israel.” Jesus himself comes near and walks with them, but their eyes are kept from recognising him. He listens to their sorrow, then opens the Scriptures: “beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted to them the things about himself in all the scriptures.”

As evening falls they beg him: “Stay with us, because it is almost evening.” At table “he took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them. Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized him.” They had heard him in the Word; they recognise him in the breaking of the bread. Emmaus is the shape of every Holy Qurbono: first the Word that sets hearts burning, then the Bread in which we know him.

The two disciples do not wait until morning. That same hour they return to Jerusalem to tell the others: “The Lord has risen indeed.” A heart that has met the risen Lord cannot stay silent. Peter and John say the same before the council in Acts: “we cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”

St Paul reminds us that this is all grace: “by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.” Jesus walks with us on our roads of disappointment, even when we do not recognise him. He waits to be invited: “Stay with us.”
conn: Moses and the prophets.
Jesus reads the whole Old Testament as pointing to him (Luke 24:27): the reason our lectionary reads Law and Prophets every Sunday.
The breaking of the bread.
Took, blessed, broke, gave: the words of the Last Supper (Luke 22:19) and of every Qurbono.
Another form.
Mark 16:12: the risen Lord appears “in another form”; we must learn to recognise him.
I was ready to be found.
Isaiah 65:1: God seeks those who were not seeking him.
altar: The Liturgy of the Word and the Holy Qurbono are Emmaus repeated every Sunday: our hearts burn as the Scriptures are opened, and our eyes are opened at the breaking of the bread.
outline: Walking away from Jerusalem: our disappointments.
Even unrecognised, the Lord is near.
The Word opened: read Scripture with Christ as its key.
Point 3 · Known in the breaking of the bread
live: Read the Gospel daily
Read the Sunday Gospel each day this week and ask Jesus to open it to you.
Invite him
Pray each evening: “Stay with us, Lord, for it is evening.”
Tell someone
Share with one person a time when you felt the Lord walking with you.
fathers: They did not recognise him while he explained the Scriptures; they recognised him in the breaking of the bread. So we too, who do not see him in the flesh, recognise him in the breaking of the bread (Sermon 235).
They invited the stranger to share their home, and found God; by hospitality they came to know the One they had not known in the explanation of the Scriptures (Homilies on the Gospels 23).
magis: Catechism 1346–1347
The Eucharistic liturgy unfolds like the Emmaus meal: the Word, then the breaking of bread.
Dei Verbum 21
The Church has always venerated the Scriptures as she venerates the Body of the Lord, offering the bread of life from the table of the Word and of the Body.
Verbum Domini 54
The Emmaus story shows the unity of Word and Eucharist.
saints: 23 Apr: St George, Martyr. 25 Apr: St Mark, Evangelist (falls on Sunday in 2027).
2027-04-18.prayer: Lord Jesus, you walked with the disciples of Emmaus and made their hearts burn as you opened the Scriptures. Walk with us on our roads, open the Word to us, make yourself known in the breaking of the bread, and stay with us, for it is evening. Amen.

2027-04-25.title: Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: Go and make disciples of all nations
In a time of favour I have answered you
A new creation; ambassadors for Christ
You are witnesses of these things
2027-04-25.alt: Season of Qyomtho. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was Syro-Malankara Catholic Laity Day. Today is also the feast of St Mark the Evangelist.
2027-04-25.verse: And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
theo: The risen Lord stands among his frightened disciples: “Peace be with you… Why are you frightened, and why do doubts arise in your hearts? Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself.” He eats before them. Then “he opened their minds to understand the scriptures”: the Messiah had to suffer and rise, and “repentance and forgiveness of sins is to be proclaimed in his name to all nations… You are witnesses of these things.”

In the evening Gospel the risen Christ gives the great commission on a mountain in Galilee: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything that I have commanded you. And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.” The Church exists to evangelise.

Peter discovers in the house of Cornelius that “God shows no partiality”: the Gospel is for every nation. St Paul calls every Christian an ambassador: “if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation… So we are ambassadors for Christ, since God is making his appeal through us.” This is why the Church honours the laity today: the mission is not only for priests and religious, but for every baptised person in family, work and society.

Job's fortunes were restored when he prayed for his friends; Solomon received wisdom when he asked for it. Let us ask the risen Lord for the wisdom and courage to be his witnesses, knowing that he is with us always.
conn: To all nations.
Isaiah 49:6, “a light to the nations”, is fulfilled when the risen Christ sends his disciples to all peoples (Luke 24:47; Matthew 28:19).
Touch and see.
The risen body is real: hands, feet, eating fish (Luke 24:39–43). The Resurrection is not a vision.
A new creation.
2 Corinthians 5:17: in Christ the new creation begun on Easter morning reaches every believer.
Prayer for friends.
Job 42:10: Job is restored when he prays for the friends who had wronged him.
altar: At the end of every Holy Qurbono the priest blesses and sends us out. That dismissal is the great commission: we leave the altar as witnesses, with the promise “I am with you always.”
outline: Touch and see; he eats with them.
Christ is the key to the Scriptures.
The great commission belongs to all the baptised: Laity Day.
Point 4 · I am with you always
live: Be an ambassador (2 Corinthians 5:20)
Speak one word of faith or hope to a colleague or neighbour this week.
Serve in the parish
Offer your time to one parish ministry or lay association.
Pray for missionaries
Pray for priests, sisters and lay missionaries from Kerala working in North India and abroad.
fathers: Christ showed them his wounds so that the marks of the nails and the spear might heal the wounds of unbelieving hearts (Sermon 73 on the Ascension, 2).
He did not say “I will be with you only”, but “with all who believe after you”; he spoke to all the faithful as to one body (Homilies on Matthew 90).
magis: Apostolicam Actuositatem 2–3
The Christian vocation is by its nature a vocation to the apostolate; the laity share in the priestly, prophetic and kingly office of Christ.
Christifideles Laici 15
The lay faithful are called to sanctify the world from within, in family, work and society.
Catechism 849–856
The missionary mandate: the Church is sent to all nations.
saints: 25 Apr: St Mark the Evangelist. 29 Apr: St Catherine of Siena. 1 May: St Joseph the Worker. 2 May: St Athanasius of Alexandria.
2027-04-25.prayer: Risen Lord Jesus, you opened the minds of your disciples and sent them to all nations. Open our minds to the Scriptures, make us your ambassadors in our families and work, and keep us faithful to your promise: I am with you always. Amen.

quick: The risen Lord gives peace, mission, the Spirit and forgiveness.
Thomas' doubt becomes the great confession: “My Lord and my God!”
Blessed are those who have not seen and yet believe: that is us.
2027-04-04.action: Say “My Lord and my God” at the elevation in every Qurbono.
2027-04-04.question: Where are the locked doors in my life that Jesus wants to enter?
2027-04-04.special: New Sunday: the appearance of the risen Lord to the apostles and to Thomas.
illus: Pilgrims at the shrine of St Thomas in Mylapore kneel and whisper “My Lord and my God.” A faith that crossed seas from a doubting apostle's touch has lasted nearly two thousand years in our land.

family.explain: Thomas did not believe Jesus had risen until he saw him. When Jesus showed him his hands and side, Thomas said: “My Lord and my God!” Thomas later came to India to tell people about Jesus.
family.intention: We thank God for St Thomas who brought the faith to India.
family.ask: Ask: “Why do we call ourselves St Thomas Christians?”

catechism: The apostles meet the risen Lord.
kidsaint: He wanted to see before believing, but when he met the risen Jesus he said: “My Lord and my God!” Tradition says he brought the Gospel to India. Lesson: bring your questions to Jesus; he helps you believe.
term: The Sunday after Qyomtho, also called Thomas Sunday, when the Church reads the appearances of the risen Lord to the apostles and to Thomas (John 20:19–29).
termMore: The ancient Christians of Kerala trace their faith to the preaching of St Thomas. The Syro-Malankara and Syro-Malabar Churches both belong to this heritage.

quick: The risen Lord meets us in our empty nights.
“Come and have breakfast”: he feeds us at his table.
“Do you love me?”: love restores us after failure.
2027-04-11.action: Each night this week, tell Jesus: “Lord, you know that I love you.”
2027-04-11.question: Have I let a failure stop me from following Jesus?
illus: Fishermen on Kerala's coast know nights when the boats come back empty. Then a call comes: “Fish to the north!” and the nets come back full. The disciples knew that morning; the risen Lord still turns our empty nights into full nets.

family.explain: The disciples caught nothing all night. Jesus told them where to throw the net, and it became full of fish! Then Jesus made them breakfast on the beach.
family.intention: We pray for fishermen and for all who work hard and feel they have failed.
family.ask: Ask: “When have we felt that we failed, and how did God help us?”

kidsaint: He denied Jesus three times, but Jesus forgave him and asked three times: “Do you love me?” Peter became the leader of the Church. Lesson: when you fail, come back to Jesus and say “I love you.”
term: The fifty days from Easter to Pentecost, kept as one great feast of the Resurrection. Its Sundays read the appearances of the risen Lord.
termMore: Many of the apostles were fishermen. After the Resurrection Jesus meets them at their work and makes them “fishers of people” for good.

quick: Jesus walks with us even when we do not recognise him.
Our hearts burn in the Word; our eyes open in the breaking of the bread.
Meeting the risen Lord, we cannot keep silent.
2027-04-18.action: Read the Sunday Gospel every day this week.
2027-04-18.question: On which road of disappointment do I need to recognise Jesus walking beside me?
2027-04-18.special: Third Sunday after Qyomtho: the disciples of Emmaus.
illus: A Kerala nurse working abroad felt lost and stopped going to church. One evening a stranger from her parish town invited her to an Indian Qurbono nearby. When the priest broke the bread, she wept: “I felt I was home.” Emmaus happens still.

family.explain: Two sad friends walked with a stranger who explained the Bible to them. When he broke bread at supper, they saw it was Jesus! They ran back to tell everyone.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel sad or lost, that they may meet Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Where did we feel Jesus close to us this week?”

catechism: Scripture in the life of the Church.
kidsaint: He wrote the shortest Gospel, full of action, so that people everywhere could know Jesus. His Gospel tells how the risen Jesus appeared to two disciples on the road. Lesson: read a little of the Gospel every day.
term: A village about eleven kilometres from Jerusalem, where two disciples recognised the risen Lord in the breaking of the bread (Luke 24:13–35). The story is a picture of every Holy Qurbono.
termMore: The Fathers spoke of two tables in the liturgy: the table of the Word and the table of the Body of Christ. Both nourish us.

quick: The risen Lord is real: “Touch me and see.”
“Go and make disciples of all nations”: every baptised person is sent.
“I am with you always, to the end of the age.”
2027-04-25.action: Speak one word of faith or hope to a colleague or neighbour this week.
2027-04-25.question: Where is the Lord sending me as his witness this week?
2027-04-25.special: Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho. Feast of St Mark. (In 2025–26 also Laity Day; check the collection.)
illus: A Kerala teacher in a government school never preached, but her honesty, patience and care for poor students made colleagues ask: “Why are you like this?” She answered simply: “Because of Jesus.” That is lay apostolate.

family.explain: Before going back to the Father, Jesus told his friends: “Go and tell everyone about me. I am with you always.” He says this to us too!
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and for courage to tell others about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family show Jesus' love to our neighbours?”

catechism: The vocation of the lay faithful.
kidsaint: A Jesuit missionary who came to India and travelled along the coasts, baptising thousands and teaching children their prayers. He went as far as Japan. Lesson: Jesus sends each of us to share his love.
term: In the 2025–26 lectionary the Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho is Syro-Malankara Catholic Laity Day, when the Church prays for the lay faithful and supports their works.
termMore: Christ's last command in Matthew (28:18–20): go, make disciples, baptise, teach. It is the charter of the Church's mission.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on the evening of Easter the disciples were behind locked doors, full of fear. Jesus came and stood among them: “Peace be with you.” He showed them his wounds. Then he sent them: “As the Father has sent me, so I send you.” He breathed on them: “Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven.”

Thomas was not there, and he would not believe: “Unless I see the marks of the nails and put my hand in his side, I will not believe.” A week later Jesus came again and invited him: “Put your finger here; reach out your hand. Do not doubt, but believe.” And Thomas cried out: “My Lord and my God!”

Dear friends, this is our own family story. Thomas, who doubted and then believed, brought this faith to India. We are called St Thomas Christians. His doubt, healed by the wounds of Christ, became our faith. In many of our churches people whisper his words when the priest lifts up the holy Mysteries: My Lord and my God.

Jesus then said: “Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.” That is you and me. We have not seen him, but we love him. Let us not live behind locked doors of fear. Let us bring our doubts to his wounds, receive his peace, and go out as witnesses. My Lord and my God! Amen.
kids: Children, after Jesus rose, Thomas said: “I won't believe unless I see him myself!”
A week later Jesus came and said: “Thomas, look at my hands.” Thomas fell down and said: “My Lord and my God!”
Thomas later came to India to tell people about Jesus. That's why we are St Thomas Christians! Let's say together: “My Lord and my God!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, after Easter Peter says, “I am going fishing,” and six others go with him. They work all night and catch nothing. Many of us know such nights: hard work with nothing to show for it, prayers that seem unanswered, plans that fail.

At dawn a stranger calls from the shore: “Cast the net to the right side.” They do, and the net is full. John cries, “It is the Lord!” and Peter jumps into the water. On the beach Jesus has a fire going, with fish and bread. “Come and have breakfast.” The risen Lord cooks for his tired friends. That is our God: he meets us in our failures and feeds us.

After breakfast, beside the fire, Jesus asks Peter three times: “Do you love me?” Three times, because three times Peter had denied him by another fire. Jesus does not scold him; he lets love heal the wound. “Lord, you know that I love you.” “Feed my sheep.” Peter, forgiven, is made the shepherd of the Church.

Whatever your failures, Jesus asks you the same question today: “Do you love me?” Answer him honestly. And let your love become service: feed his lambs, in your family, your parish, your work. Every Holy Qurbono he says again: “Come and have breakfast.” Amen.
kids: Children, the disciples went fishing all night and caught nothing. In the morning a man on the beach said: “Throw your net on the right side!” And the net was full of fish!
It was Jesus! He had made breakfast for them on the beach. Then he asked Peter: “Do you love me?” Peter said: “Yes, Lord, you know I love you!”
Jesus asks you too: “Do you love me?” What will you say? Let's say: “Jesus, I love you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on Easter afternoon two disciples are walking away from Jerusalem, sad and disappointed. “We had hoped that he was the one,” they say. Many of us walk such roads: disappointed with life, with the Church, with God. And then a stranger joins them.

It is Jesus, but they do not recognise him. He lets them pour out their sorrow. Then he opens the Scriptures, from Moses and all the prophets, and shows them that the Messiah had to suffer and enter his glory. Later they will say: “Were not our hearts burning within us while he was opening the scriptures?”

As evening falls they invite him in: “Stay with us.” At table he takes bread, blesses it, breaks it and gives it to them, and their eyes are opened. This is exactly what happens at every Holy Qurbono: the Word sets our hearts on fire; the breaking of the bread opens our eyes. Emmaus is not just a story; it is our Sunday.

And they could not keep it to themselves. In the dark they ran back seven miles to Jerusalem to tell the others: “The Lord is risen!” Let us read the Gospel each day this week, invite Jesus into our homes, and tell someone what he has done for us. Stay with us, Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, two friends of Jesus were walking home, very sad. A stranger walked with them and explained the Bible. Their hearts felt warm!
At supper the stranger broke the bread, and suddenly they saw: it was Jesus! Then he disappeared.
They ran all the way back to tell their friends! When the priest breaks the bread at Qurbana, Jesus is there too. Let's say: “Jesus, stay with us!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the disciples are gathered, frightened and confused, when the risen Jesus stands among them: “Peace be with you. Why are you frightened? Look at my hands and my feet; it is I myself.” He even eats a piece of fish in front of them. The Resurrection is not a ghost story; the Lord is truly alive, body and soul.

Then he opens their minds to understand the Scriptures, and gives them a task: repentance and forgiveness of sins must be proclaimed in his name to all nations. “You are witnesses of these things.” In Matthew he says it on a mountain: “Go therefore and make disciples of all nations… And remember, I am with you always.”

This command is not only for priests and sisters. St Paul says every Christian is “an ambassador for Christ”. Today our Church honours the laity, because most of the world will never hear a sermon from a priest; they will only see Christ in you: in your honesty at work, your patience at home, your kindness to the poor, your courage to say “I am a Christian.”

Job was restored when he prayed for his friends. Solomon received wisdom when he asked. Let us ask the risen Lord for wisdom and courage, and go out from this Qurbono as his witnesses. He has promised: “I am with you always, to the end of the age.” Amen.
kids: Children, before Jesus went back to heaven, he gave his friends a big job: “Go and tell everyone about me!”
And he made a promise: “I will be with you always.” Jesus is with us every day, at school, at home, everywhere.
You can tell others about Jesus by being kind and honest. Let's say: “Jesus, I will be your helper!”

intro: Theme: “Peace be with you: sent, forgiven, believing.”
On New Sunday the Risen Lord comes through locked doors. He gives peace, breathes the Spirit, entrusts the power to forgive sins, and leads Thomas from doubt to faith.

sub: The disciples hide in fear; Jesus comes and stands among them.
His first word is “Peace”, not reproach.
Isaiah tells the herald of good tidings: “lift up your voice … do not fear.” The Risen Christ turns fear into mission.
q: Get you up to a high mountain, O Zion, herald of good tidings; lift up your voice with strength, O Jerusalem, herald of good tidings, lift it up, do not fear.

When it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors of the house where the disciples had met were locked for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
points.apply: Bring your fears to the Risen Lord in prayer; let him say to you: “Peace be with you.”

points.h: Sent with the Spirit to forgive
sub: Elisha asked for a double share of Elijah's spirit to continue his mission.
Jesus breathes on the apostles: “Receive the Holy Spirit.”
He gives them power to forgive sins: the gift of the sacrament of Reconciliation.
q: Elisha said, “Please let me inherit a double share of your spirit.”

Jesus said to them again, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, so I send you.” When he had said this, he breathed on them and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them.”
points.apply: Make an Easter confession if you have not yet done so.

points.h: Blessed are those who have not seen
sub: The Lord does not abandon doubting Thomas; like a shepherd he comes back for the one.
He shows his wounds; Thomas confesses: “My Lord and my God!”
We are among those blessed who believe without seeing.
q: He will feed his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms, and carry them in his bosom, and gently lead the mother sheep.
Then he said to Thomas, “Put your finger here and see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it in my side. Do not doubt but believe.” Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”
points.apply: At the elevation in the Qurbono, say silently: “My Lord and my God.”

concl: Peace, Spirit, mercy and faith: these are the gifts of the Risen Lord on New Sunday.
Let us receive them and become messengers of his peace.
2027-04-04.resolve: Forgive one person this week, as Christ forgives you.

intro: After the Resurrection the disciples go back to fishing on the lake. All night they catch nothing. At dawn a stranger tells them where to cast the net, and they recognise him. He has prepared breakfast for them.

sub: Peter says “I am going fishing”: back to the old life.
“That night they caught nothing”: our efforts without the Lord bear little fruit.
The Psalmist knew it: unless the Lord builds the house, the builders labour in vain.
q: Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.
Simon Peter said to them, “I am going fishing.” They said to him, “We will go with you.” They went out and got into the boat, but that night they caught nothing.
points.apply: Begin each workday this week with a short prayer offering your work to God.

sub: At dawn Jesus stands on the shore; they do not recognise him.
They obey: “Cast the net to the right side”, and the net is full.
The beloved disciple sees with the eyes of love: “It is the Lord!”
q: The LORD is my strength and my might, and he has become my salvation; this is my God, and I will praise him.

He said to them, “Cast the net to the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they cast it, and now they were not able to haul it in because there were so many fish. That disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!”
points.apply: Where have you failed recently? Try again, this time at his word and with prayer.

sub: The Risen Lord has lit a fire and prepared bread and fish.
He takes the bread and gives it to them: the gesture of the Eucharist.
“Taste and see that the Lord is good”: in the Qurbono he still feeds tired disciples.
q: O taste and see that the LORD is good; happy are those who take refuge in him.
Jesus said to them, “Come and have breakfast.” … Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and did the same with the fish.
points.apply: Come to Holy Qurbono this week not as a duty but as an invitation from a friend.

concl: The Risen Lord meets us in our ordinary work and our empty nights.
Let us obey his word, recognise him with love, and come to his table.
2027-04-11.resolve: Share a meal this week with someone who is lonely.

intro: Two disappointed disciples walk away from Jerusalem. The Risen Lord walks with them unrecognised, opens the Scriptures, and is known in the breaking of the bread. Emmaus is the shape of every Holy Qurbono: Word, Bread, Mission.

points.h: He walks with us in disappointment
sub: “We had hoped …”: they walk away sad, their hopes buried.
Jesus comes near and walks with them, though they do not recognise him.
God seeks even those who are not seeking him.
q: I was ready to be sought out by those who did not ask, to be found by those who did not seek me. I said, “Here I am, here I am.”
While they were talking and discussing, Jesus himself came near and went with them, but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
points.apply: Tell the Lord honestly about your disappointments; he is walking with you.

sub: Beginning with Moses and all the prophets, Jesus explains the Scriptures about himself.
Their hearts burn within them: the Word prepares for recognition.
In the Qurbono the readings and homily are this road to Emmaus.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
They said to each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us while he was talking to us on the road, while he was opening the scriptures to us?”
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel at home before you come to church.

points.h: Known in the breaking of the bread
sub: “Stay with us, because it is almost evening”: they invite him in.
He takes bread, blesses, breaks and gives: their eyes are opened.
At once they return to Jerusalem to tell the others: every Qurbono ends in mission.
q: Come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed.
When he was at the table with them, he took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them. Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized him.
points.apply: After Qurbono, share the joy of faith with one person at home or at work.

concl: The Lord walks with us, speaks to us and feeds us.
Let us say each day: “Stay with us, Lord,” and run to tell others that he is risen.
2027-04-18.resolve: Pray each evening this week: “Stay with us, Lord, for it is evening.”

intro: The Risen Lord shows the disciples his hands and feet, opens their minds to the Scriptures, and sends them to all nations. The Gospel of this Sunday is the Church's charter of mission.

points.h: “Look at my hands”: a real, risen Lord
sub: The disciples are frightened and think they see a ghost.
Jesus shows his wounds: the Risen One is the Crucified One, truly alive in his body.
God never forgets us: our names are inscribed on the palms of his hands.
q: Can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you. See, I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands.
He said to them, “Why are you frightened, and why do doubts arise in your hearts? Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself.”
points.apply: In moments of fear this week, look at a crucifix and remember: he has not forgotten you.

sub: God revealed himself to Moses as merciful and gracious.
Repentance and forgiveness are to be proclaimed in Christ's name to all nations.
Peter learns that God shows no partiality: every nation is welcome.
q: The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness.
Then Peter began to speak to them: “I truly understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.”
points.apply: Reject every prejudice against people of other castes, languages or religions.

sub: God made his Servant a covenant for the people.
All authority is given to Jesus; he sends us to baptise and teach.
He does not send us alone: “I am with you always, to the end of the age.”
q: In a time of favor I have answered you, on a day of salvation I have helped you; I have kept you and given you as a covenant to the people.

Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything that I have commanded you. And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Support the missions with prayer and an offering; teach the faith to the children in your family.

concl: The Risen Christ shows his wounds, opens the Scriptures, forgives and sends.
Let us be his witnesses, confident that he is with us always.
2027-04-25.resolve: Pray for missionaries, especially those from Kerala serving in other lands.
